heading: INT. LIBRARY OF THE OLD MILL HOUSE - EVENING

units.text: INT. LIBRARY OF THE OLD MILL HOUSE - EVENING
A long, low room under a timbered ceiling.
Shelves of leather books, a fire crackling in a stone hearth, a rain-streaked window overlooking the mill race.
A grandfather clock stands against the wall, stopped at ten past four.
INSPECTOR CORNELIA VANDERHOEK-ASANTE (50s, gray tweed, a pipe she never lights) paces slowly, studying the shelves.
Two suspects sit in leather chairs by the fire, each with a glass of sherry untouched at their elbow.
LADY OTTILIE FAIRBROTHER-ZULU (70s, silver rings on every finger) sits bolt upright, spine like a ruler.
Beside her, the housekeeper, MRS. AGATHA PENHALIGON-DUBOIS (60s, apron still tied, hands folded in her lap) stares at the floor.
Thank you all for waiting.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: We had little choice, Inspector.
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: No. You didn't.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: She stops at a shelf.
Runs a finger along the spines.
Pulls one out, holds it up, replaces it.
This is absurd. My brother Reginald fell down the stairs.
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: He did. Eventually.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: The poor man.
units.name: MRS. PENHALIGON

units.text: Mrs. Penhaligon, you found the body at six?
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: Quarter to six, ma'am. The clock was already stopped.
units.name: MRS. PENHALIGON

units.text: At ten past four.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: It's been stopped for years.
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: No, Lady Fairbrother. It was stopped this morning. The pendulum is still warm.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: Silence.
The fire pops.
Ottilie's hand tightens on the arm of her chair.
Someone stopped it at ten past four to give themselves an alibi.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: Who would do that?
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: Someone who forgot the clock has a second winding key.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: The door opens, and a young constable, DENNIS HOLLOWAY-PARK (20s, rain-slick cape), comes in holding a small brass key in a handkerchief.
Found it, Inspector. In the pocket of the dead man's dressing gown.
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: Thank you, Constable.
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: She takes the key, turns it over, and looks at each of them in turn.
Ottilie meets her gaze.
And Mrs. Penhaligon, very slowly, lifts her eyes.
It's mine, ma'am.
units.name: MRS. PENHALIGON

units.text: Agatha --
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: It was always going to come to this, my lady.
units.name: MRS. PENHALIGON

units.text: Mrs. Penhaligon, would you come with me?
units.name: CORNELIA

units.text: She nods, rises, smooths her apron, and walks to the door without looking back.
